title: Vader 4 Pro user manual
source: Official Flydigi Vader 4 Pro Gaming Controller User Manual (bundled PDF)

blocks.text: Rotate the force adjustment knob around each stick to change damping continuously.

items: Clockwise → more damping: steadier aim and precise control.
Counterclockwise → less damping: freer movement, less hand fatigue.

blocks.alt: Force adjustment ring around the right stick (MIN / MAX)

blocks.text: Use this app over USB or the wireless dongle to remap buttons, set keyboard shortcuts and macros, tune stick and trigger feel, and change lighting. Bluetooth is great for play; plug in a cable or the dongle when you want to save settings.

items.title: Buttons
items.text: Remap controls, keyboard keys, combos, macros, and turbo.

items.title: Feel
items.text: Deadzones, response limits, and motor strength.

items.title: Firmware
items.text: Check for updates and install over USB or the dongle.

items: Plug the dongle into a USB port on your computer.
Set the rear mode switch to the dongle (USB) position.
Press Home on the controller — it pairs automatically. The indicator stays white.
Later sessions: press Home again and it reconnects.

blocks.text: Set the rear switch to the dongle (USB) position. Connect with a USB cable. A solid white indicator means the link is up.

items: Set the rear switch to the Bluetooth position.
Press Home to wake the controller.
In your computer’s Bluetooth settings, connect to “Xbox Wireless Controller”.
A solid white indicator means it connected.

blocks.text: XInput is the usual mode for most games (hold Home+X; white indicator). It emulates a standard Xbox controller, which is what the majority of titles expect.
Use DInput when you want proper gyro / motion sensing (hold Home+A; blue indicator). XInput does not expose the pad’s real gyro — only Xbox-style controls — so motion features need DInput.

On Linux, lighting and settings work in DInput over USB or the 2.4 GHz dongle. If the pad is in XInput mode, games still see a normal Xbox-style controller. Bluetooth is fine for play; plug in a cable or the dongle when you want to change lighting or save mappings.

items: On the Switch home screen open Controllers → Change Grip/Order.
Set the rear mode switch to NS.
Press Home once — the controller connects. The indicator stays blue.
Later sessions: press Home again to reconnect.

blocks.text: Face buttons follow Nintendo layout (A/B and X/Y swapped vs Xbox). Select / Start become − / +. Home is still Home; the Capture / Screenshot control maps to the Switch screenshot button.

items: Set the rear switch to Bluetooth.
Press Home to wake the controller.
Enable Bluetooth on the phone/tablet and connect to “Xbox Wireless Controller”.
Indicator stays white when linked. Later: press Home to reconnect.

blocks.text: That path is for games with native controller support. For titles without gamepad support on Android, use Flydigi Game Center → Peripheral management → switch to controller mode.

rows: Change the rear mode switch (or auto-off after ~15 minutes idle).

blocks.text: XInput is the main PC mode for game compatibility (Xbox-style). Prefer DInput when you need real gyro — XInput does not expose it properly. On Linux, use DInput with USB or the dongle for lighting and settings.

blocks.a: Confirm the rear mode switch matches the link you want. Hold Home for about three seconds until the indicator flashes quickly to enter pairing mode. Dongle: unplug and reseat the receiver. Bluetooth: forget the device, toggle Bluetooth, then reconnect.
Open the Firmware page in this app, check for updates, and install over USB or the wireless dongle. Keep the cable or dongle connected until the update finishes.

blocks.q: Joystick, trigger, or motion sensing feels wrong.
blocks.a: Open Feel and recheck deadzones and response limits. If it still feels off, follow the calibration steps in Flydigi’s official online manual, then fine-tune Feel again.
